title: To Learn, Retrieve
heading: To Learn, Retrieve
coreClaim: The chapter argues that retrieving information from memory strengthens learning and should be treated as part of the learning process rather than only as a later measurement.
distinctMechanism: The mechanism is reconstruction from memory: low-stakes quizzes and self-testing pressure recall, expose weakness, and make later access stronger when the learner corrects and repeats.
requiredAnchors: Retrieval practice strengthens learning better than repeated exposure alone.
Self-quizzing and low-stakes testing can improve retention.
Missed recall should trigger correction and another attempt rather than surrender.
commonMisreadings: Getting answers wrong means retrieval is not working.
specificApplications: Use low-stakes quizzes or blank-page summaries during review.
Add retrieval checks to classroom or workplace practice.
Repair misses and retrieve again instead of stopping at the first failure.
hardEdgeRequirement: Keep retrieval productive by preserving support, feedback, and repair instead of treating struggle as self-justifying.
thresholdQuestion: How do you turn a retrieval miss into stronger learning instead of empty frustration?
